audits.title: 91 Mrs Bad Bones: Impact of COVID-19 on Secondary Prevention of Fragility Fractures
audits.standard: not reported
audits.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic unit, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire

cycle1.period: Pre- and post-UK lockdown (dates not given)
cycle1.result: Pre-lockdown vs lockdown: orthogeriatric review 88% to 0%; vitamin D/calcium 81.6% to 58.0% (p = 0.0156); bone-sparing medication 60.7% to 18.2% (p = 0.0037); DEXA requests 40.1% to 3.6% (p = 0.0027).

audits.intervention: Introduction of the 'MRS BAD BONES' mnemonic for secondary fracture prevention.

audits.title: Improving Osteoporosis Management in Primary Care: An Audit of the Impact of a Community Based Fracture Liaison Nurse.
audits.standard: Anticipated pay-for-performance (QOF/Directed Enhanced Service) osteoporosis indicators: register of patients with fragility fracture, and treatment with a bone-sparing agent in those aged 50–74 with confirmed osteoporosis and in those aged 75 and over with a fragility fracture
audits.setting: 12 general practices in Crawley, south-east England; primary care, community-based fracture liaison nurse pilot

cycle1.result: Females 50–74 (n=13,519) and ≥75 (n=4,883). Bone-sparing agent in those aged 50–74 with fragility fracture and confirmed osteoporosis 47.9% (23/48); in those ≥75 with fragility fracture 39.5% (118/181). Fragility fracture recorded 8.8% (15/171) aged 50–74 and 0.8% (65/8110) aged ≥75.

audits.intervention: Introduction of a community-based fracture liaison nurse who reviewed the practice population meeting the inclusion criteria.

cycle2.result: Bone-sparing agent 84.0% (42/50) aged 50–74 and 70.5% (222/316) aged ≥75 (p<0.001). Fragility fracture recorded 14% (25/178) aged 50–74 (p=0.168) and 2.3% (199/8702) aged ≥75 (p<0.001).

audits.other_findings: Recording of smoking and BMI roughly doubled, but DXA scan recording fell (e.g. 2.5% to 1.4% in those ≥75); less deprived patients were more likely to receive DXA scans and more deprived patients bone-sparing agents.

audits.title: Secondary Prevention of Hip Fragility Fractures During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Service Evaluation of "MRS BAD BONES".
audits.standard: UHCW trust guidelines (in line with NICE) for secondary fragility fracture prevention: vitamin D/calcium supplementation, bone-sparing medication, DEXA scan for eligible patients, bone blood tests including PTH
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic department, University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire (major trauma centre)

cycle1.period: Patients admitted immediately before the UK lockdown of 23 March 2020 (study period February to June 2020)
cycle1.result: Pre-lockdown baseline: orthogeriatric review 88% (44/50); vitamin D/calcium 40/49 (81.6%); bone-sparing medication 17/28 (60.7%); DEXA requested 9/22 (40.1%); PTH measured 5 (10%). Post-lockdown (n=50, before intervention): orthogeriatric review 0%; vitamin D/calcium 29/50 (58.0%, P=.02); bone-sparing medication 4/22 (18.2%, P=.004); DEXA 1/28 (3.6%, P=.003).

audits.intervention: Audit results presented at the monthly T&O quality improvement meeting and the 'MRS BAD BONES' mnemonic disseminated to junior doctors, advanced nurse practitioners and medical students

cycle2.period: After dissemination of the mnemonic (within February to June 2020)
cycle2.result: Vitamin D/calcium 42/49 (85.7%, P=.003 vs post-lockdown); bone-sparing medication 21/29 (72.4%, P<.001); DEXA requested 12/21 (60.0%, P<.001); orthogeriatric review 38% (19/50).

audits.other_findings: PTH was measured in no patients after lockdown or after the intervention. The return of the orthogeriatric team during the post-intervention phase is a confounder.
audits.citation: Stephens A, Rudd H, Stephens E, Ward J. Secondary Prevention of Hip Fragility Fractures During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Service Evaluation of "MRS BAD BONES". JMIR Aging. 2020;3(2):e25607. doi:10.2196/25607. PMID: 33326412.

audits.title: Improving Secondary Bone Protection Prescription in Patients Admitted With a Femoral Neck Fracture.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Hip Fracture Database: all patients with hip fracture assessed for and managed with a secondary bone-protection plan (100% gold standard); SMART aim of an additional 40% per year
audits.setting: Orthopaedic wards of a large district general hospital with a level 2 trauma centre

cycle1.result: 13.9% (n=11) assessed for bone protection; 1.3% (n=1) prescribed a bisphosphonate and 10.1% (n=8) other bone protection; 86.1% (n=68) neither assessed nor prescribed.

audits.intervention: PDSA 1 awareness poster (January 2019); PDSA 2 education session for clerking and ward doctors added to induction (March 2019); PDSA 3 MDT meeting with responsibility charting, giving assessment and prescribing to the care of the elderly team (April 2019).

cycle2.period: April 2019 (a fortnight after the MDT meeting)
cycle2.result: 100% (n=50) of patients assessed or placed on a bone-protection plan.

audits.other_findings: PDSA 1 (n=27) 44.4% (p<0.01) and PDSA 2 (n=21) 76% (p<0.001); an annual re-audit of 50 patients during the COVID-19 pandemic showed 100% was sustained. At baseline 89.9% of patients and relatives were unaware of bone protection.
audits.citation: Hamid M, Chikhlia A, Gogna A. Improving Secondary Bone Protection Prescription in Patients Admitted With a Femoral Neck Fracture. Cureus. 2021;13(10):e18883. doi:10.7759/cureus.18883. PMID: 34820213.

audits.title: Improving referrals to a fracture liaison service: Screening for osteoporosis.
audits.standard: Recommended FLS guidelines: referral of patients meeting age criteria with first fragility fracture
audits.setting: Orthopaedic practice with internal Fracture Liaison Service, Southeastern United States

cycle1.result: 5% FLS referrals.

audits.intervention: Alert button in the electronic health record prompting surgeons to refer eligible patients to FLS.

cycle2.result: 19% FLS referrals (14% improvement).

audits.other_findings: not reported
audits.citation: McDowell SL, Freeman JC. Improving referrals to a fracture liaison service: Screening for osteoporosis. Int J Orthop Trauma Nurs. 2022;47:100964. doi:10.1016/j.ijotn.2022.100964. PMID: 36423534.

audits.title: A Five-Year Retrospective Audit on Bone Protection Prescribing in Patients With Fragility Fractures in Primary Care.
audits.standard: NICE guidance on bone protection (bisphosphonates first line) after fragility fracture
audits.setting: Mansell Road Practice, primary care general practice, London

cycle1.result: 33/47 on bone protection agents (26 bisphosphonate plus calcium/vitamin D, 7 bisphosphonate alone); 2 on calcium/vitamin D alone; 12/47 on neither therapy.

audits.intervention: Educational poster on recognition and coding of fragility fractures; untreated patients reviewed individually and started on treatment, referred for DEXA or specialist advice.

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Of the 12 untreated, 2 were miscoded; of the remaining 10, 4 were referred for DEXA, 2 referred for zoledronic acid and 1 started alendronic acid. No re-audit reported.
audits.citation: Redman IA, Sivanesan V. A Five-Year Retrospective Audit on Bone Protection Prescribing in Patients With Fragility Fractures in Primary Care. Cureus. 2023;15(9):e45532. doi:10.7759/cureus.45532. PMID: 37731682.

audits.title: A Retrospective Audit of Osteoporosis Management Following Fragility Fractures in a Hospital Setting.
audits.standard: Six Standards of Hip Care (assessment for antiresorptive medication after fragility fracture) and NOGG UK 2021 guidance; NICE recommendations on vitamin D and bone protection
audits.setting: Warrington Hospital, district general hospital; inpatients aged 65 and over with fragility fractures

cycle1.result: Inpatient bisphosphonates started in 23/144 (16%); 105/121 (87%) not started by GP after discharge; FRAX recorded in 78/144 (54%); vitamin D assessed in 89/144 (62%) and replaced in 78/144 (54%); 110/144 no DEXA scan; 34/144 (25%) referred to metabolic bone clinic

audits.intervention: Teaching sessions, MDT meetings and bedside teaching; local protocol flowcharts; push to start antiresorptives before discharge; new orthogeriatrics SHO role; new older people osteoporosis clinic

cycle2.result: 105/165 (64%) did not receive appropriate bisphosphonates (34 started as inpatients); 104/131 (around 80%) not started by GP after discharge; FRAX recorded in 30/165 (18%); vitamin D checked in 57/165 (35%) and 99/165 (60%) received no replacement; DEXA and bone clinic referrals remained low

audits.other_findings: Only minor improvement in inpatient bisphosphonate prescribing; the osteoporosis clinic opened about six months late. Patients discharged from the emergency department were often not assessed, so an SOP and electronic alerts were proposed.
audits.citation: Singh S, Patil S, Thein M, Kulkarni J, Kakroo AZ, Singh L, et al.. A Retrospective Audit of Osteoporosis Management Following Fragility Fractures in a Hospital Setting. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e76047. doi:10.7759/cureus.76047. PMID: 39711942.

audits.title: International benchmarking of secondary fracture prevention in older adults with hip fracture: a Chinese hospital-based KPI audit.
audits.standard: UK Fracture Liaison Service Database (FFFAP) key performance indicators (7 of 11 KPIs assessed), benchmarked against UK FFFAP 2016–2018 figures
audits.setting: Orthogeriatric co-managed ward, Beijing Jishuitan Hospital, tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: BMD screening 97.1% (2,610/2,689); bone-protective medication before discharge 94.0% (2,454/2,610); follow-up 50.7% at 90 days, 17.7% at 12–16 weeks, 9.5% at 12 months. 2018 KPIs: FLS assessment within 90 days 57.1% (UK 67.0%), falls assessment 87.5%, bone therapy recommended 94.3%, adherence at 12 months 11.6% (UK 18.8%).

audits.intervention: not reported

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Falls assessment rose from 11.4% (2016) to 87.5% (2018) and DXA-only scanning fell to 14.1% in 2018 as QCT replaced it. Secondary fracture rates stayed at 11.0–13.4% across follow-up points.
audits.citation: Yuan Y, Wang W, Li PY, Zhang M, Lu YN, Yang MH, et al.. International benchmarking of secondary fracture prevention in older adults with hip fracture: a Chinese hospital-based KPI audit. Front Health Serv. 2026;6:1799272. doi:10.3389/frhs.2026.1799272. PMID: 42221965.

audits.title: An audit of post fracture rehabilitation with special emphasis on osteoporosis assessment and treatment.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians guidelines and Department of Health osteoporosis guidelines
audits.setting: Devonshire Royal Hospital, Buxton; rehabilitation after referral from orthopaedic departments

cycle1.result: Care met Royal College of Physicians guidelines; previous fractures in 17 and osteoporosis risk factors in 16 patients; osteoporosis assessment and treatment per DOH guidelines lacking.

audits.intervention: not reported

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Mortality 4%; 9/44 previously living at home needed residential or nursing home placement.
audits.citation: al-Allaf AW, Pal B, Reid N. An audit of post fracture rehabilitation with special emphasis on osteoporosis assessment and treatment. Clin Exp Rheumatol. 1998;16(4):451-453. PMID: 9706426.

audits.title: An audit of osteoporotic patients in an Australian general practice.
audits.standard: Royal Australian College of General Practitioners osteoporosis guidelines
audits.setting: Rural medical centre, 10 general practitioners (New South Wales)

cycle1.result: Only 35% had been scanned for osteoporosis; 66% with osteopenia and 26% with osteoporosis were receiving no treatment; 48% with previous low BMD had not had recommended follow-up scans.

audits.intervention: not reported

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Scanning rates varied with age, gender and number and type of risk factors; active surveillance with PENCAT suggested.
audits.citation: Parker D. An audit of osteoporotic patients in an Australian general practice. Aust Fam Physician. 2013;42(6):423-427. PMID: 23781552.
